sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: This lesson pulls together the core building blocks from Units 1–9: the 1st/2nd-person forms of lenni ('to be') — vagyok, vagy — question words like Ki? ('who?'), Mi? ('what?') and Hol? ('where?'), the plural ending -k, and possessive endings like -m ('my').

Vagyok and vagy are the 1st- and 2nd-person forms of lenni ('to be') and are always spoken aloud — it's only the 3rd person that Hungarian drops (ő Anna, not ő van Anna), so don't extend that omission back onto yourself or 'you'.
